summary.headline: Finolex Q4 FY26 EBITDA nearly doubled to INR332 crore on inventory gains and VCM-linked margins, but volumes stayed flat at 101,772 tonnes.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,314 crore, with EBITDA up to INR332 crore from INR171 crore and PBT up 65% to INR334 crore. Volumes were broadly flat YoY at 101,772 tonnes, as agri demand did not pick up in Q4 and farmers held back on expectations of lower prices. Management attributed part of the margin jump to an inventory gain of about INR35-40 crore and to backward-integration fuel cost advantages, and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to sub-15%. The company guided FY27 volume growth of higher single digit to lower double digit on a full-year basis.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR171 crore in Q4 FY25 (nearly doubled)
Up YoY; analyst-calculated ~22% ex inventory gain
vs INR144 crore in Q4 FY25

Flat vs INR4,142 crore in FY25

segments.name: PVC pipes (agri vs non-agri)
segments.commentary: Agri was about 63% of FY26 mix versus 67% in FY25; management's ideal long-run split is 50:50 over 4-5 years. Agri is about 65-70% of volume per CFO, and Q4 saw agri volume fall while non-agri rose.

segments.name: Fittings
segments.commentary: Fittings were about 9% of Q4 volume (9% in Q4 FY25) and about 11% of FY26 volume (10% in FY25). Fitting volume growth is around 9-10%.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7-8% of overall volume in Q4 (6-7% a year ago) and CPVC portfolio volume is growing about 8-9%; CPVC fittings grow faster.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin target is sub-15% (mid to lower double digit), described as conservative given geopolitical uncertainty; management expects to deliver higher margin toward year-end.
FY27 volume growth target of higher single digit to lower double digit on a full-year basis, not quarterly.
Q1 FY27 margin not guided; April was subdued and management will assess May and June.
Maintenance and debottlenecking capex of roughly INR100 crore per year, with extruder upgrades; capacity is 520,000 tonnes and sufficient for current and probably next year's volume.
Dividend decision on accumulated cash (about INR2,563 crore net cash) is pending with the Board; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity rose to 520,000 tonnes in FY26 from 492,000 tonnes at end FY25.
FY26 capacity utilisation was about 67% (71% in FY25), per CFO.
Management says capacity is not a constraint; growth will be supported by replacing lines with higher-capacity extruders.
Annual capex around INR100 crore for maintenance plus debottlenecking; no new greenfield or multi-location plant announced.

VCM supply: Middle East was a major VCM source; the company is shifting sourcing to Far East and Northeast Asia, and the monsoon shutdown of the VCM line for 4-5 months means no VCM run-rate impact in that period.
demand_pricing: April 2026 demand was subdued after prices peaked in March and then fell; May was somewhat better, and agri demand returned ahead of the monsoon.
Current agri demand is about 25-27% below the March price peak, per management.
Q4 PVC/EDC spread averaged $521/t versus about $793 average international PVC; current PVC/EDC spread is about $543 with international PVC near $900+.
PVC/VCM spread is currently about $108 versus about $179-180 average in Q4, a sharp fall that management acknowledged will weigh on the quarter.
Government imposed a 90-day import duty on PVC resin from April to 30 June 2026; management said ADD is not viable now, while MIP is a possible short-term option being pursued by CPMA.
Monsoon is delayed in Kerala by about 7-10 days and a lower-than-normal monsoon is forecast; management says agri losses will be partly offset by non-agri growth.

qa_highlights.question: What was the inventory gain in Q4, and is the margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about INR35-40 crore from March-April price rises; management said margin is at the higher side and will moderate, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided to sub-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume flat in Q4 when peers reported restocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri volume fell because farmers expected prices to soften after the spike; non-agri volume rose, and total volume stayed flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall and finance cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income fell to about INR36 crore from about INR52-58 crore on lower mark-to-market gains on investments; finance cost rose to about INR7.8 crore from INR3 crore as the company built inventory and borrowed against it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company return surplus cash to shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board has not yet decided on the use of accumulated cash; the FY26 dividend came from current accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Does the VCM supply from the Middle East threaten PVC resin output in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the monsoon shutdown of the VCM line covers 4-5 months anyway, and that the company is switching to Far East and Northeast Asia sources, so no availability impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide sub-15% margin when the 10-year average is about 17.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance is conservative because of geopolitical uncertainty and that the company expects to deliver higher margin toward year-end.

risks_watch: Monsoon timing and strength, which drives agri demand (about 63% of FY26 mix); a lower monsoon is already forecast.
PVC/VCM spread compression (from about $179 to $108) could weigh on Q1 FY27 margins, and inventory gains may reverse.
Middle East supply disruption for VCM and polymer price volatility.
Import duty on PVC resin expires 30 June 2026; any MIP or ADD decision is pending.
Volume growth lagging peers; FY26 volume fell about 4.4%.
Finance cost rising due to inventory-linked borrowing; other income falling as mark-to-market gains decline.
Capital allocation of about INR2,500+ crore of net cash remains undecided.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the Q4 numbers and the balance sheet but cautious on forward margins and volumes, repeatedly citing monsoon, PVC price volatility and Middle East supply risk. It was evasive on the cash return timeline, on the agri-versus-non-agri margin gap, and on capacity expansion plans, saying the Board has not decided.
key_quotes: So this is near-term positive for integrated producers like us, but the supply uncertainty and cost inflation remains a risk, but which we continue to monitor very, very closely.
Overall, the kind of margin that we have -- you have seen during the current quarter is obviously certain at the higher side, but going to be -- going forward, it is going to moderate to some extent.
So we don't want to give any rosy picture at this moment because of the geopolitical scenario, the future is always see uncertainty.
So capacity is not a constraint for the growth.

adds.what: Installed capacity rose to 520,000 tonnes in FY26 from 492,000 tonnes at end FY25 (extruder replacement/debottlenecking; already live)

growth.why: FY27 volume growth guided at higher single digit to lower double digit (full year), with EBITDA margin sub-15%; backing is mainly existing 520,000 t capacity at 67% utilisation plus agri/non-agri demand recovery, with no specific new orders or capacity timing, so clarity is vague.
